name: Pop the Question
tagline: Plan a proposal they'll retell for decades
about: Pop the Question plans a marriage proposal end to end: ideas matched to your partner's personality, a run sheet with backups, the words you'll say, how to talk to their family, and a ring brief that doesn't overspend.
persona: You are a discreet proposal planner and friend: you match the moment to the person, plan for rain and nerves, and never push spending beyond what's sensible.

onboarding.title: Make the moment theirs
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us about your partner and roughly when you're thinking.
bullets: A run sheet with a Plan B
The words, the family, the ring

profile.label: Your story in one line
profile.placeholder: met at a climbing gym in 2021, first trip to Lisbon

tools.title: Proposal ideas
tools.subtitle: Five ways, ranked by fit
tools.prompt: Suggest 5 proposal ideas for the profile partner and story: setting {setting}, budget {budget}, privacy '{privacy}'. Cards (meta = cost · effort · weather-dependent yes/no), each naming the exact moment the question gets asked; then bullets ranking them by fit with the partner's personality with one line on why; then a callout on ideas to avoid for this personality (no jumbotron for the private type).

tools.title: The run sheet
tools.subtitle: Timings, accomplices, Plan B

inputs.label: The plan
inputs.placeholder: sunset at Primrose Hill, picnic, her sister hiding with a camera

tools.prompt: Turn this plan into an operation: {plan} on {date}. Sections: a table (Time | Action | Who | Backup) from the morning to after the yes; a checklist for the week before (ring insured and sized, accomplices briefed, photographer, bookings, phone charged, nails if they'd want photos); a callout on Plan B for rain, a late train or a bad-mood day; and a quote with the exact message to send accomplices.

tools.title: What I'll say
tools.subtitle: Your voice, no clichés

inputs.label: What you love, moments, promises
inputs.placeholder: the way she laughs at her own jokes; the night we got lost in Porto; I want to…

tools.prompt: Write a {length} proposal speech from: {notes}, in the user's plain voice (no clichés, no 'from the moment I saw you'). A quote with the full speech ending in the question; a second quote with a 2-line version for when nerves erase the script; and bullets on delivery (kneel or not, when the ring comes out, breathe, wait for the answer).

tools.title: Ask the family
tools.subtitle: Blessing, heads-up or both

inputs.label: Anything tricky
inputs.placeholder: her dad is old-fashioned; we've only met twice

tools.prompt: Help with asking or telling {who}, where the family is '{culture}' and: {concerns}. Steps for how and when to do it (in person, call, what to lead with); a quote with a script for the conversation including answers to 'why now' and 'what if they say no'; bullets on cross-cultural or divorced-parent nuance where relevant; and a callout on keeping the secret after the conversation.

tools.title: Ring brief
tools.subtitle: Style, size, sensible spend

inputs.label: Clues
inputs.placeholder: wears silver not gold, thin bands, allergic to nickel

tools.prompt: Brief the ring for {style} style at {budget} using clues: {clues}. Sections: kv (metal, setting, stone options including lab-grown and non-diamond, band width, estimated price range); a table (Priority | Spend here | Save here); steps for finding the ring size without asking (borrow a ring, trace it, ask a friend, resizing allowance); and a callout on returns, insurance and ignoring the 'months of salary' rule invented for marketing.

disclaimer: Ring and budget notes are general guidance, not financial advice; get sizing and stone certification from a jeweller.
